machine: darwin arm64, node v22.22.0, Apple M4

rows.input: Delta compression has been a mess: one dropped packet desyncs a client until the next full state, and players on mobile networks see rubber-banding every few seconds. Match state moves to full snapshots at 20 Hz with client-side interpolation.
rows.line: Delta compression has been a mess: one dropped packet desyncs a client until the next full state, and players on mobile networks see rubber-banding every few seconds.

rows.input: The server-side anti-cheat plugin has cost us more than it saves: it adds 3 ms to every tick at 64 players and flagged a dozen legit players for fast movement on high-refresh monitors. It comes out; we'll use post-match statistics instead.
rows.line: The server-side anti-cheat plugin has cost us more than it saves: it adds 3 ms to every tick at 64 players and flagged a dozen legit players for fast movement on high-refresh monitors. It comes out

rows.input: One row per match in Postgres stopped working at our volume: the inserts at the end of a big tournament lock the table for seconds and the leaderboard page times out. Match history moves to an append-only event table that a job rolls up into the leaderboard every minute.
rows.line: One row per match in Postgres stopped working at our volume: the inserts at the end of a big tournament lock the table for seconds and the leaderboard page times out.

rows.input: The drift is gone in 1.13, but its UDP socket wrapper copies every packet into a new buffer, and at 64 players that took the tick from 11 ms to 19 ms, over the 16 ms budget. I went back to tokio.
rows.line: The drift is gone in 1.13, but its UDP socket wrapper copies every packet into a new buffer, and at 64 players that took the tick from 11 ms to 19 ms, over the 16 ms budget. I went back to tokio.

rows.input: Retried Quinn now that we have a relay for NAT. The timeouts are gone, but QUIC's congestion control halves our send rate on every lost packet, and on lossy mobile links the match state arrives in bursts. Staying on our UDP channel.
rows.line: Retried Quinn now that we have a relay for NAT. The timeouts are gone, but QUIC's congestion control halves our send rate on every lost packet

rows.input: I tried bincode's varint encoding for the state packets. Packets got about 30% smaller, but encoding took 2.4 ms per tick at 64 players against 0.9 ms for the fixed-width format, which pushes the tick past 16 ms in busy fights. I reverted to fixed-width.
rows.line: I tried bincode's varint encoding for the state packets. Packets got about 30% smaller, but encoding took 2.4 ms per tick at 64 players against 0.9 ms for the fixed-width format

rows.input: I tried moving pathfinding for the bots to a rayon thread pool. It made each bot's path about four times faster, but the pool stole cores from the tick thread and the p99 tick went from 12 ms to 21 ms on the 8-core boxes. Pathfinding stays on the tick thread with a budget per frame.
rows.line: Moving pathfinding for the bots to a rayon thread pool. It made each bot's path about four times faster

rows.input: The Google Calendar webhook channels keep expiring after a week and we miss the renewals, so staff calendars silently stop syncing and double bookings follow. Calendar sync moves to a nightly full import plus a pull every 15 minutes.
rows.line: The Google Calendar webhook channels keep expiring after a week and we miss the renewals, so staff calendars silently stop syncing and double bookings follow.

rows.input: Computing availability on every request doesn't hold up anymore: the big salons have 40 staff and the widget takes 3 seconds to show a day, and customers leave. Availability moves to a slots table that the schedule and booking actions keep up to date.
rows.line: Computing availability on every request doesn't hold up anymore: the big salons have 40 staff and the widget takes 3 seconds to show a day, and customers leave.

rows.input: Horizon on our single Redis has bitten us twice: when Redis ran out of memory during the spring promo, queued confirmation jobs were evicted and 300 customers never got their booking email. Jobs move to SQS; Redis stays for cache only.
rows.line: Horizon on our single Redis has bitten us twice: when Redis ran out of memory during the spring promo, queued confirmation jobs were evicted and 300 customers never got their booking email.

rows.input: I tried Octane with the singleton fixed: sessions are fine now, but the PDF invoice generator leaks about 40 MB per request under Swoole, so the workers hit their memory limit within an hour. Back on PHP-FPM.
rows.line: I tried Octane with the singleton fixed: sessions are fine now, but the PDF invoice generator leaks about 40 MB per request under Swoole, so the workers hit their memory limit within an hour.

rows.input: We retried the SMS aggregator with sender ID registration done. Delivery in Ireland is fine now, but every message came from a different short code, so customers couldn't reply to reschedule and their replies were lost. Reminders stay on email.
rows.line: We retried the SMS aggregator with sender ID registration done. Delivery in Ireland is fine now, but every message came from a different short code

rows.input: I tried caching the dashboard's booking counts in Redis for five minutes. The page loaded in 300 ms instead of 2 s, but staff saw bookings they had just made missing from the counts, and two salons called support thinking bookings had failed. I removed the cache; the counts query needs an index instead.
rows.line: Caching the dashboard's booking counts in Redis for five minutes. The page loaded in 300 ms instead of 2 s, but staff saw bookings they had just made missing from the counts

rows.input: I tried Laravel's model pruning for old bookings. It kept the table small, but it also deleted bookings that invoices still referenced, and the accountants' exports broke for last year. Pruning is off until the invoices keep their own copy.
rows.line: I tried Laravel's model pruning for old bookings. It kept the table small, but it also deleted bookings that invoices still referenced, and the accountants' exports broke for last year. Pruning is off

rows.input: The incremental merge on the sales facts keeps missing late POS uploads: stores that sync a day late land after the merge window, and the daily totals come out 2 to 3% low until someone runs a full refresh. Sales facts go back to a full rebuild every night.
rows.line: The incremental merge on the sales facts keeps missing late POS uploads: stores that sync a day late land after the merge window, and the daily totals come out 2 to 3% low

rows.input: The 60-second query timeout for Looker hasn't worked: the regional managers' year-over-year dashboard needs about 90 seconds on Mondays and just shows an error. Looker gets its own warehouse and a 5-minute timeout.
rows.line: The 60-second query timeout for Looker hasn't worked: the regional managers' year-over-year dashboard needs about 90 seconds on Mondays and just shows an error.

rows.input: Running dbt from Airflow every hour has been painful: the Airflow worker runs out of memory parsing our 900 models and whole hours of runs get skipped without an alert. dbt moves to dbt Cloud jobs; Airflow only triggers them.
rows.line: Running dbt from Airflow every hour has been painful: the Airflow worker runs out of memory parsing our 900 models and whole hours of runs get skipped without an alert. dbt moves to dbt Cloud jobs

rows.input: I tried it on the events table again. The store filters are fast now, but maintaining the search access path costs about 40 credits a day on that table, more than the queries it speeds up, so I turned it off.
rows.line: I tried it on the events table again. The store filters are fast now, but maintaining the search access path costs about 40 credits a day on that table, more than the queries it speeds up

rows.input: Retried the Python forecast model with a warm warehouse. The cold start is gone, but Snowpark's pandas API ran out of memory with the full three-year history, so the forecast stays in the batch job.
rows.line: Retried the Python forecast model with a warm warehouse. The cold start is gone, but Snowpark's pandas API ran out of memory with the full three-year history, so the forecast stays in the batch job.

rows.input: I tried clustering the inventory table on store and day. Queries scanned about 70% fewer partitions, but automatic reclustering cost more credits than the scans saved, around 25 a day, because the POS sync touches every store each hour. I dropped the clustering key.
rows.line: Clustering the inventory table on store and day. Queries scanned about 70% fewer partitions, but automatic reclustering cost more credits than the scans saved, around 25 a day

rows.input: I tried materializing the marketing funnel as a dynamic table. It refreshed within a minute of new data, but it rebuilt the whole table on every refresh because of a window function the incremental refresh can't handle, and the bill tripled. It's a nightly table again.
rows.line: Materializing the marketing funnel as a dynamic table. It refreshed within a minute of new data, but it rebuilt the whole table on every refresh
